title: Partition Existing Table
description: Learn how to partition an existing table in SQL Server using T-SQL.

data.text: Partitioning an existing table involves creating filegroups, a partition function, a partition scheme, and a clustered index on the partition scheme.
Steps to Partition an Existing Table

items: Create filegroups to hold the partitions.
Create a partition function to define partition boundaries.
Create a partition scheme to map partitions to filegroups.
Create a clustered index on the partitioning column based on the partition scheme.

data.content: Creates a partition function that splits orders by year.

data.text: Step 4: Create a Clustered Index on the Partitioning Column

To partition the orders table by the order_date column, you need to create a clustered index on the partition scheme. This requires removing the existing primary key and foreign key constraints temporarily.

data.title: Partition the Orders Table
data.content: Drops constraints, creates partitioned index, then restores constraints.

data.title: Partition Existing Table Key Points
points: Partitioning improves query performance and maintenance for large tables.
Create filegroups, partition function, and partition scheme before partitioning.
The partition column must be part of a clustered index.
Use transactions to safely partition existing tables with foreign key constraints.
